title: Affine chain representative of a specified bottom arrow
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $a\in\mathbf Z$, $M$ an $\mathcal O_T$-module sheaf and $f:M[-a]\to D$ an arrow invertible on $H^a$. Choose derived-category localizations for all schemes in one morphism universe. Let $U\subset T$ be open and let $K$ be a cochain complex of module sheaves on $U$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], bounded above, zero below $a$, with $d^a=0$ and finite free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Fix $e:L(U\hookrightarrow T)^*D\cong Q(K)$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. For every $x\in U$ there is an affine open $W\subset U$ containing $x$, bounded-above finite-free complexes $A,B$ on $W$ with $A^i=0$ for $i\ne a$, $B^i=0$ for $i<a$ and $d_B^a=0$, and a chain map $\alpha:A\to B$ invertible on $H^a$, together with isomorphisms $e_A:L(W\hookrightarrow T)^*(M[-a])\cong Q(A)$ and $e_B:L(W\hookrightarrow T)^*D\cong Q(B)$ satisfying $L(W\hookrightarrow T)^*f\,e_B=e_AQ(\alpha)$.

source.place: Second proof, local chain representatives; 0BDL zero-bottom chart and 0D5S derived composition

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood W of x contained in U using Mathlib.exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset. For each open immersion, identify tensor pullback with exact restriction by uniqueness of left adjoints. The exact restriction functor induces a functor on derived categories; its factorization is a left-derived counit by Functor.isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_inverts. Uniqueness of left derived functors gives a natural comparison with derivedPullback. Restrict K termwise along W → U to obtain B; restriction preserves zero objects and finite free sheaves (Modules.restrictFreeIso), hence the bounds and zero bottom differential. Use Modules.restrictFunctorComp along W → U → T, Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, and Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso to identify the restriction to W with restriction to U followed by restriction to W. Combine these natural comparisons with e and the restriction/localization factorization to obtain eB. General composition or coherence of derived pullbacks is unnecessary.

Naturality of the derived restriction comparison and Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso transfer hf to the restricted arrow. Both differentials in the short complex of B at degree a are zero, so ShortComplex.HomologyData.ofZeros identifies its homology with B.X a. Compose these comparisons with the single-complex homology isomorphism to identify R(M) with B.X a. Define A as the actual single complex on B.X a in degree a; its off-degree terms are zero, hence isomorphic to the rank-zero free sheaf. Its degree-a term is finite free by the corresponding property of B. The restriction/single-functor comparison gives eA.

Transport A and B to the localized site using the inverse of Modules.overEquiv W. Choose the standard derived localization there (its morphism universe need not equal w); the induced derived equivalence is full. Preservation of zero objects, the unit comparison Modules.overEquivFunctorObjUnitIso, and SheafOfModules.mapFreeIso give strictly perfect transported complexes. Lift the conjugated specified arrow along the full induced derived functor, and apply perfect_affine_map_representative. Transport the resulting chain map back, conjugate by the counit comparison for the complexes, and use naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors to prove its Q-image equals the specified arrow. Naturality of DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors then transfers the invertible bottom homology of the conjugated restricted arrow to H^a(alpha). Cancel eA to obtain the required square.

proof_origin.note: N1 realizes the three-step local chain construction; composition is obtained from ordinary exact restrictions instead of the general derived-composition theorem. Exact-open naturality is proved privately using uniqueness of left derived functors; no object-only homology comparison is imported. Affine-site transport and homology invertibility are proved using the existing affine representative theorem and Mathlib functoriality.

lean.statement:
theorem zeroBottomArrow_affine_chain_model
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (D : schemeDerivedCategory T) (a : ℤ)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace))
    (f : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) a).obj M ⟶ D)
    (hf : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) a).map f))
    (U : T.Opens)
    (K : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ c : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, c < i → IsZero (K.X i))
    (hnegative : ∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (K.X i))
    (hzero : K.d a (a + 1) = 0)
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (K.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin n))))
    (e : (derivedPullback U.ι).obj D ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)
    (x : T) (hx : x ∈ U) :
    ∃ W : T.Opens, x ∈ W ∧ W ≤ U ∧ IsAffineOpen W ∧
      ∃ A B : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace)) ℤ,
        (∃ c : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, c < i → IsZero (A.X i)) ∧
        (∃ c : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, c < i → IsZero (B.X i)) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (A.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
          (R := moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (B.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
          (R := moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ a → IsZero (A.X i)) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (B.X i)) ∧ B.d a (a + 1) = 0 ∧
        ∃ α : A ⟶ B, IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap α a) ∧
          ∃ (eA : (derivedPullback W.ι).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) a).obj M) ≅
                DerivedCategory.Q.obj A)
            (eB : (derivedPullback W.ι).obj D ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj B),
            (derivedPullback W.ι).map f ≫ eB.hom =
              eA.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map α
